clips.title: The thinking lever
clips.why: Anthropic's own advice on choosing an effort level, which is the exact setting Byte's route changes.
look: Effort trades quality against cost and time; it is a choice per task, not a global setting.
When low effort is enough, and when the extra thinking pays for itself.
Measure on your own tasks instead of guessing: our BYTE-GOLD slice per route.
clips.after: Byte's route is this advice written as a function: low for docs, tests and dependencies, high for big PRs, medium for the rest, each proved on BYTE-GOLD.

clips.title: Extended Thinking Explained — Effort, Thinking Tokens, and What You're Paying Claude for Thinking
clips.why: A short, concrete look at what effort costs and how to choose it in code.
look: Current models use effort levels, not a fixed thinking budget.
When the extra thinking pays off and when it is waste.
Effort routing in code: choose the level per request, as Byte's gate does per PR.
clips.after: In Byte the choice reaches the worker as one flag, --effort, which the gate sets from the PR's files.

clips.title: Let AI review draft PRs before a human does: Unblocked's risk-based code review workflow
clips.channel: Unblocked | Context layer for agentic software dev
clips.why: Another team's version of the same idea: an AI review on draft PRs that gives each PR a risk level before a person is notified.
look: The PR starts as a draft, and the AI reviews it first.
A risk score decides how much human attention the PR needs.
The person is notified only at the end, with the risk in front of them.
clips.after: Byte's risk label does the informing part, but it never changes who approves: every fcp PR still needs one human approval, never from the requester.

clips.title: Small vs. Large AI Models: Trade-offs & Use Cases Explained
clips.why: When a smaller, cheaper setting is the right tool, explained without any vendor details.
look: Small models fit narrow, well-defined tasks.
Cost and speed matter most when the task runs very often.
Compare with Byte: a review runs on every push of every PR.
clips.after: Byte moves effort instead of model size for reviews, but the reasoning is the same, and the panel later uses Sonnet 5.5 for its simplest lens.

practice.q: A PR changes only frontend/src/components/ProjectsTable/ProjectsTable.test.tsx, 300 lines. Which effort?

options.why: Every counted file is a test, so the PR is test-only.
Medium is for ordinary code under 400 lines. A test-only PR is one of the low kinds.
300 lines is under 400, and test-only wins anyway.

practice.q: Complete the rule that raises a PR's risk tier by size.
practice.hint: There is no tier above it.
practice.why: A PR that is already high cannot go higher; low becomes med and med becomes high.

practice.q: What does the Byte risk check do on a risk:high PR?

options.text: Fails, so the PR cannot merge until two people approve
options.why: The check is neutral and never required. The approval rules stay exactly the same.

options.text: Finishes as neutral and lists the matched rules, so the reviewer knows where to look
options.why: It informs the one reviewer and never decides anything.

options.text: Passes once Byte's review is clean
options.why: The risk check does not depend on the review. It is computed from the paths and size alone.

practice.q: Put what happens when a PR is opened in fcp in order.
items: The gate lists the PR's changed files with their additions and deletions
reviewRoute picks the effort, leaving lockfiles out
riskFor picks the tier from Byte's own policy, and the label and neutral check are set
reviewMode sends risk:high or very large PRs to the panel
The review runs, and its route and reason show in the status comment
practice.why: All three decisions come from the same file list, before any model call.

practice.q: A new route (medium effort for ordinary PRs) loses 5 points of recall on high bugs on its BYTE-GOLD slice. What happens?

options.text: It ships anyway, because it halves the cost
options.why: Cost never buys missed bugs. The bar is within 3 points.

options.text: That route goes back to high effort
options.why: Each route stays only while its slice holds. This one did not.

options.text: The whole routing feature is removed
options.why: Only the route that lost goes back. Low effort for docs-only PRs can still stay.
